h1: Does malt go stale? Malt freshness and shelf life explained
title: Malt Freshness and Shelf Life Explained | Craft Beer School
desc: Does malt go stale? How long whole and crushed malt keep, how to spot stale or damp malt and how to store it in Indian heat and humidity.
teaser: Malt does not have a hard expiry date, but it does lose crispness, pick up moisture and go stale. Here is how to tell.
standfirst: Malt is dried grain, so it keeps far longer than hops or yeast. It still changes over months, faster once it is crushed and much faster in a humid room. Here is how long it lasts and how to check a sack before brew day.
sections: Malt is dry for a reason

Malt leaves the maltings very dry, typically around 4% to 5% moisture. That dryness stops mould and slows the chemistry that turns flavour stale. Malt draws water from the air, so in a damp room it slowly creeps up. As moisture rises, the grain loses its crisp snap, becomes harder to mill well and, in bad cases, goes musty or mouldy.

The certificate of analysis from the maltster tells you the moisture when it left. Everything after that is your storage.

Whole base malt in sealed sacks, kept cool and dry, generally stays in good brewing condition for many months and often a year or more. Specialty malts are similar, although crystal malts can turn sticky in humid air. Dark roasted malts are fairly robust.

Crushed malt is a different matter. Milling exposes the starchy inside to air and moisture. Most brewers use crushed malt within a couple of weeks and sooner in the monsoon. If your homebrew shop mills for you, buy close to brew day.

None of these are hard limits. Storage conditions decide more than the calendar does.

• Bite a kernel. Fresh malt is crisp and crunchy with a sweet, bready taste. Damp or slack malt is chewy.
  • Smell it. Fresh malt smells of bread, biscuits or toast. Musty, damp or cardboard smells mean trouble.
  • Look at it. Clumps, grey or green fuzz, webbing or insects mean the malt is not usable.
  • Check the date. Write the date received on every sack or bag when it arrives.

Malt with visible mould should be thrown away. Mould can produce toxins and the flavour will carry into the beer.
What stale malt does to beer

Slightly old but dry malt usually brews fine, perhaps with a little less extract and a duller malt aroma. Malt that has picked up moisture gives poorer crush quality, lower efficiency and can add a stale, grainy or papery note that no hop schedule hides. Over time, beer brewed from tired malt also tends to stale faster in the package, since beer staling chemistry starts with what goes into the mash.
Storing malt at home in India

1. Keep whole grain until brew day if you have a mill.
  2. Store it in airtight food containers or heavy, sealed buckets, not the open paper sack.
  3. Keep it off the floor, away from the kitchen steam and out of sunlight.
  4. In the monsoon, a few food-safe silica gel packs in the container help. Check them and replace when saturated.
  5. Label each container with malt name and date received. Use oldest first.

Weevils and grain moths love malt. Tight lids keep them out. If they are already in the house, keep malt in sealed containers in the coolest room you have.
Crystal and specialty malts in the heat

Crystal and caramel malts have glassy, sugary centres that pull in moisture faster than base malt. In a humid kitchen they can clump and turn chewy within weeks of opening. Roasted malts handle storage better, but their aroma fades over time, so a stout brewed from a bag of chocolate malt opened a year ago can taste duller than you expect.

Keep opened specialty malts in small, well-sealed jars and buy them in the smallest packs that make sense for your brewing. A cool cupboard on the inside wall of the house is better than a shelf near a window or the kitchen stove.

Bulk buying looks cheaper per kilo. For a homebrewer making a batch a month, a 25 kg sack of base malt can be gone in a few months, which is fine. A 25 kg sack of a specialty malt you use 200 g at a time may outlast its freshness. Split sacks with brewing friends or buy specialty malts in small packs.

Knowing your base malts well also helps here. When you understand what each one brings to the beer, you can substitute from what you have rather than stockpile every malt a recipe ever mentioned.

Freshness is one of those topics that sounds minor until a batch tastes flat for no obvious reason. Tracking ingredient dates in your brew log is how you rule it in or out.
faqs: Not on a fixed date, but it slowly loses quality. Whole malt kept cool, dry and sealed generally stays good for many months and often a year or more.
How long does crushed malt last?
Use it within a couple of weeks. In humid weather, sooner. Crushing exposes the grain to air and moisture.
How can I tell if malt has gone bad?
Bite a kernel and smell it. Chewy, musty, mouldy or insect-damaged malt should not be used.
Dry old malt is usually just less flavourful. Malt with visible mould should be discarded.
